accepted.title: Three normal generators for Epstein’s relation subgroup
accepted.text: Let F=F(a,b,c,d), and let R be the normal closure in F of [a,b], b², [c,d], d³. Can R be normally generated in F by three elements? Equivalently, can the marked presentation of (ℤ×ℤ/2)*(ℤ×ℤ/3) on a,b,c,d be replaced by three defining relators?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: Held PDF footer, physical page; extraction pages inflated by4

accepted.scope_review: Marked generators fixed. A three-generator relation module is known; this is normal generation of the relation subgroup, not merely generation of R/[R,R].
accepted.literature_finding: Held source and Harlander primary relation-gap lecture retain the Epstein example. Fresh Epstein/relation-gap searches found no proof that this R is normally3-generated or requires4.

accepted.title: Four-relator cores detecting commutativity from coprime powers
accepted.text: For coprime positive integers m,n let F=F(a,b), F^(r)=⟨uʳ:u∈F⟩, and Qₘ,ₙ=⟨a,b | [u,v], u,v∈F^(m); [u,v], u,v∈F^(n)⟩. For which m,n does a four-relator subpresentation of Qₘ,ₙ already present ℤ² via the natural map on a,b? In particular, for which pairs is Δₘ,ₙ=⟨a,b | [aᵐ,bᵐ],[aⁿ,bⁿ],[(ab)ᵐ,(ba)ᵐ],[(ab)ⁿ,(ba)ⁿ]⟩ isomorphic to ℤ²?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: Held PDF footer, physical page; extraction pages inflated by4

accepted.scope_review: Finite core is a literal finite subset of the specified relators whose normal closure equals the full relator normal closure; not any arbitrary presentation of an isomorphic group. Preserve both general core and specificΔ clauses.
accepted.literature_finding: Primary2019 paper (arXiv1705.09348)§6 Questions1–2 retain both targets; the(2,3) example and bounded computations do not resolve all coprime pairs. Fresh four-relator/Gardam query found no later closure.

accepted.title: Minimum core size for nilpotency detected in power subgroups
accepted.text: For c≥1 and coprime positive m,n, set k=c+1, F=F(x₁,…,xₖ), F^(r)=⟨uʳ:u∈F⟩, and ν_c(y₁,…,yₖ)=[[…[y₁,y₂],y₃],…,yₖ]. Let Q=⟨x₁,…,xₖ | ν_c(u₁,…,uₖ), uᵢ∈F^(m); ν_c(v₁,…,vₖ),vᵢ∈F^(n)⟩. Determine the minimum cardinality of a finite subset of these relators presenting the same marked group, as a function of c,m,n.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: Held PDF footer, physical page; extraction pages inflated by4

accepted.scope_review: The infinite presentation has a finite core because it presents the free nilpotent group of classc. Size counts relators, with original generators fixed; do not replace finite core by arbitrary presentation deficiency.
accepted.literature_finding: Question2 in current primary1705.09348§6 retains this exact complexity target; explicit8-relator abelian construction is a bound, not minimality. No later exact formula located.

accepted.title: Classify laws detectable in coprime power subgroups
accepted.text: For a word w∈F(x₁,…,xₖ), say G satisfies w if w(g₁,…,gₖ)=1 for every k-tuple in G. Write G^(r)=⟨gʳ:g∈G⟩. Classify words w such that, for every group G and every pair of coprime positive integers m,n, G satisfies w whenever both G^(m) and G^(n) satisfy w.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: Held PDF footer, physical page; extraction pages inflated by4

accepted.scope_review: All groups, not just finite groups; every coprime pair. Converse is automatic because laws pass to subgroups. Distinct from determining finite cores for a known detectable law.
accepted.literature_finding: Author primary page and1705.09348§6 Question3 retain classification. Its nilpotent/locally-nilpotent results and metabelian counterexample are partial classification only. No full characterization found.

accepted.title: Automaticity of one-relator groups without unbalanced Baumslag–Solitar subgroups
accepted.text: Let G have a finite presentation with one defining relator. Suppose G contains no subgroup isomorphic to BS(m,n)=⟨a,t | t⁻¹aᵐt=aⁿ⟩ with m,n nonzero integers and |m|≠|n|. Must G be automatic: admit a finite generating set and a regular language of representatives with a synchronous fellow-traveller bound for pairs representing elements differing by a generator?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: Held PDF footer, physical page; extraction pages inflated by4

accepted.scope_review: Synchronous automaticity. Balanced BS(m,±m) are allowed. Source small census and non-CAT(0) constructions do not answer automaticity generally.
accepted.literature_finding: Gardam primary author list retains census results; current one-relator survey covers geometric improvements but no universal automaticity theorem located. Fresh CAT/automatic searches find counterexamples to biautomaticity only, which do not refute this target.

accepted.title: Polynomial-time word problem for every one-relator group
accepted.text: For every fixed finite one-relator presentation G=⟨X | r⟩, does there exist a deterministic algorithm deciding whether an input word in X∪X⁻¹ is trivial in G in time polynomial in its length?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: Held PDF footer, physical page; extraction pages inflated by4

accepted.scope_review: Presentation is fixed and the polynomial may depend on it; no uniform polynomial in relator-plus-word length is silently requested. Complexity concerns word problem, not Dehn function.
accepted.literature_finding: 2025 Linton–Nyberg-Brodda primary survey2501.18306§2.8.3 explicitly retains Question2.8.3. Known polynomial algorithms for Baumslag–Gersten groups do not settle all one-relator groups.

accepted.title: Profinite rigidity among finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifolds
accepted.text: Let M,N be connected complete finite-volume hyperbolic3-manifolds. If π₁(M) and π₁(N) have the same finite quotient groups up to isomorphism, must π₁(M)≅π₁(N), and hence must M,N be isometric?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

accepted.scope_review: Relative to finite-volume hyperbolic3-manifold groups; not absolute rigidity among all residually finite groups. The source census proves pairwise separation within a finite sample only.

accepted.title: Volume from maximal asymptotic homological torsion growth
accepted.text: For a connected complete finite-volume hyperbolic3-manifold M, put G=π₁(M). Is limsup_{[G:K]→∞} log|Tor H₁(K;ℤ)|/[G:K]=Vol(M)/(6π), where K ranges over all finite-index subgroups of G?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: Held PDF footer, physical page; extraction pages inflated by4

accepted.scope_review: All finite-index subgroups, with no imposed normality, nesting or exhaustion; this is the thesis limsup conjecture and differs from the stronger prescribed-tower approximation conjecture.
accepted.literature_finding: 2025 Ascari–Fruchter introduction retains exponential torsion-growth challenge; abundance of finite torsion summands is not rate control. Fresh volume/torsion review found no attainment of the asserted limsup for all hyperbolic3-manifolds. The known upper bound is recorded.

accepted.title: Hyperbolic 3-manifolds from index-marked abelianizations of covers
accepted.text: For a connected complete finite-volume hyperbolic3-manifold M define FIA(M)={([H₁(K;ℤ)],[π₁(M):K]):K≤π₁(M),[π₁(M):K]<∞}, where [H₁(K;ℤ)] is its abelian-group isomorphism class. If FIA(M)=FIA(N) for two such manifolds, must M,N be isometric?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: Held PDF footer, physical page; extraction pages inflated by4

accepted.scope_review: FIA is a set, not a multiset and not the lattice of finite-index subgroups; repeated isomorphism classes with the same index count once. Source Seifert counterexample lies outside hyperbolic class.
accepted.literature_finding: Gardam primaryQuestion5.1′ remains stronger than the unresolved full profinite-rigidity question; modern hyperbolic profinite literature proves special examples using stronger invariants. No general FIA rigidity closure located.
